events.headline: Baker Mayfield dislocates his right (throwing) thumb vs. Vikings; MRI Monday, rookie Jalon Daniels would start
events.detail: Mayfield hit his thumb on Blake Cashman while throwing an interception with 1:54 left in the 23-16 loss. X-rays showed no fracture, but Monday's MRI will check for hairline fractures and ligament damage. Todd Bowles said the timetable depends on the imaging and that undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who beat out Jake Browning in camp, would start for now if Mayfield cannot. Easton Stick is on the practice squad.
events.so_what: If Mayfield misses time, a rookie UDFA starter lowers the ceiling of every Tampa Bay pass catcher and pushes the offense toward the run. Do not start Daniels in a one-QB lineup. Anyone starting Mayfield needs a Week 4 fallback QB lined up.

events.headline: Breece Hall leaves Jets-Lions with a right thigh (quad) injury; Braelon Allen takes the backfield
events.detail: Hall grabbed his right thigh after being tackled at the sideline on a fourth-quarter red-zone run and did not return. He said he 'felt something' but did not know details yet. He had 13 carries for 32 yards and three catches for 23 yards before the injury. Braelon Allen handled the backfield after he left.
events.so_what: No diagnosis yet, so this is a wait-for-Monday item. If Hall misses time, Allen inherits the early-down and goal-line role and becomes a FLEX start; he is the priority handcuff add before Tuesday waivers.

events.headline: Raiders WR Jack Bech breaks his forearm vs. Saints and is headed to injured reserve
events.detail: Bech fractured his forearm in the second quarter and was ruled out early in the third. Ian Rapoport reports he is headed to IR, which means at least four games missed; the injury is not expected to end his season. He had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown through two games.
events.so_what: Bech was a depth receiver for fantasy, so the real question is where his snaps go in the Las Vegas WR room. Safe to drop unless you have an open IR slot.

events.headline: Mark Andrews returns for the second half vs. Cowboys after leaving with a hand injury
events.detail: Andrews left in the second quarter of the Ravens' game against Dallas in Rio de Janeiro with a hand injury and was listed questionable to return. He came back for the second half. He had one catch for 9 yards on three targets before leaving.
events.so_what: Returning in the same game is the best signal available; keep him in TE plans for Week 4 but read the midweek practice report, since hand injuries can limit catch volume even when a player suits up.

events.headline: De'Von Achane out with a knee injury; Hafley says it 'does not sound optimistic,' MRI Monday
events.detail: Achane exited in the first quarter of Miami's 24-10 loss at Kansas City after an 11-yard catch; the leg appeared to give out on a non-contact plant before the tackle. He was listed questionable to return, then downgraded to out. Coach Jeff Hafley said postgame the situation does not sound optimistic, and Ian Rapoport reports the fear is a major knee injury. An MRI Monday will confirm. Ollie Gordon took over and scored a 3-yard touchdown on the next drive; Jaylen Wright was Doubtful for this game with a stinger and foot injury.
events.so_what: Prepare for a long absence rather than a week-to-week one, but nothing is confirmed until the MRI. Ollie Gordon is the immediate goal-line and early-down back and the top waiver add in Miami's backfield this week; Jaylen Wright's health decides whether it is a committee. Achane was on the field for 83 percent of snaps, so the vacated role is a full one.

events.headline: Justin Jefferson ruled out vs. Buccaneers with a left ankle injury; O'Connell says he 'got close' to returning, MRI Monday
events.detail: Jefferson hurt his left ankle at the end of Minnesota's first possession in the 23-16 win over Tampa Bay and was ruled out. Kevin O'Connell said postgame that Jefferson got close to coming back in and that he does not believe the injury is severe. The ankle will be evaluated Monday with an MRI, and the Vikings are hoping for a low-ankle sprain rather than a high one.
events.so_what: The coach's tone is optimistic but it is a forecast, not a clearance. A low-ankle sprain is often a zero-to-one-week problem; a high-ankle sprain usually costs several weeks. Hold him through the MRI and plan a Week 4 fallback at WR or FLEX until the result lands.

events.headline: Jalen McMillan ruled out vs. Vikings after re-injuring his left knee in the first quarter
events.detail: McMillan torqued the same left knee that cost him most of training camp and the season opener, left in the first quarter after one target and no catches, and was ruled out for the rest of the game. Tez Johnson and rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst are the candidates for his snaps.
events.so_what: A recurring knee on a player who only returned in Week 2 makes him a bench or drop until he practices fully. Tez Johnson is the speculative add if the injury costs McMillan more time, but neither replacement has a set role yet.

events.headline: Marcus Mariota throws three TDs as Commanders upset Seahawks 33-31
events.detail: Starting for the injured Jayden Daniels, Mariota completed 19 of 31 for 183 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, and Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards late in the fourth quarter to seal it. Daniels (elbow) is week-to-week and reportedly unlikely for Week 4.
events.so_what: Three passing touchdowns at 4 points each with zero interceptions is a usable streaming line on only 183 yards, so Mariota is a legitimate bye-week or injury streamer while Daniels is out, and he adds some rushing. It also keeps Washington's pass catchers startable rather than sinking with a backup.

events.headline: Jaylen Warren runs for 127 and adds 49 receiving yards as Steelers beat Bengals 30-27
events.detail: With Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren took 17 carries for 127 yards and caught passes for 49 more; a further long run was wiped out by a holding penalty. Michael Pittman Jr. played through the foot injury in his return.
events.so_what: Warren showed he can carry a full workload when Dowdle is out, 176 scrimmage yards against a backfield split when both are healthy. Start him while Dowdle sits; once Dowdle is back, this game is the argument that Warren leads the committee rather than splits it.

events.headline: Nor'easter game plays to form: Giants beat Titans 12-7 at MetLife in rain and 40-mph gusts
events.detail: Forecast called for 83-88% rain with a sustained north wind around 18 mph and gusts to 41 mph. The game finished 12-7, the lowest-scoring result of the early window. Seahawks-Commanders, also forecast for gusts over 30 mph, instead finished 33-31.
events.so_what: A one-week weather result, not a signal: do not read either passing game, or either kicker, off this box score. Both defenses scored well under the points-allowed tiers, which is the weather talking. Jameis Winston is back to being judged on a normal-weather Week 4.

events.headline: Zay Flowers active vs. Cowboys in Rio after testing the hamstring pregame
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 26-27 items. Flowers (hamstring, Questionable) missed Week 2, returned to a limited practice Friday, and took the field early Sunday to test the hamstring. He is active for the late-window game against Dallas at Maracana Stadium, as is DT Nnamdi Madubuike.
events.so_what: He plays, so the question is volume rather than availability. A first game back from a hamstring can come with a snap count, so treat him as a WR2 with a lower floor this week rather than his usual role; Rashod Bateman loses the bump he would have had if Flowers sat.

events.headline: Michael Pittman active vs. Bengals; foot injury not on the Steelers' inactive list
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Pittman was limited all week with a new foot injury and listed Questionable. The Steelers' official inactives (Joey Porter Jr., Rico Dowdle, Gabriel Rubio, Kevin Jobity, Drew Allar, Eli Heidenreich) do not include him.
events.so_what: Pittman is a start in his usual flex role. Limited practices all week mean some snap-count risk, so he is a floor play rather than a ceiling one.

source.label: CBS Sports live inactives tracker, Sept. 27

events.headline: D.J. Moore and Keon Coleman active vs. Chargers after game-time-decision tags
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Both Bills receivers carried Questionable tags (Moore shoulder, Coleman ankle) and both are active on Sunday's list. Moore has not missed a game since 2020. Winds around 16-17 mph are forecast in Buffalo, short of a sit-worthy level.
events.so_what: Start Moore wherever he was your WR2/flex; no need for a pivot. Coleman stays a flex dart, not a lock, since the ankle may cap his snaps.

league_notes.clash: Moore and Coleman are both DrGMoney's.

events.headline: Tyjae Spears active vs. Giants; Tony Pollard already cleared
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Spears (ankle) carried a Questionable tag and is active. Pollard was off the final report. The game at MetLife is forecast for heavy rain and gusts to 41 mph (see weather item).
events.so_what: Pollard remains the Titans back to start; the weather favors the run game. Spears is a change-of-pace flex only in the deepest league (Couples Clash).

events.headline: Mike Evans carted off with a rib strain vs. Cardinals and ruled out; full evaluation Monday
events.detail: Evans played through his Questionable hip tag but took a big hit from Budda Baker in the second quarter, was carted to the locker room and ruled out. NFL Network reports a rib strain, with a full evaluation Monday. He had three catches for 34 yards and a touchdown before leaving, and entered the week leading the 49ers with 103 receiving yards.
events.so_what: Rib injuries are pain-tolerance questions and he is also managing the hip, so a missed Week 4 is realistic. Line up a WR or FLEX replacement now rather than waiting on Friday's report.

events.headline: Tyson Bagent cleared from the concussion protocol, no designation for Monday; Case Keenum still expected to start vs. Eagles with Caleb Williams out
events.detail: The Bears announced Sunday that Bagent is out of the concussion protocol and carries no injury designation for Monday night. Caleb Williams remains out with a hamstring injury. Bagent missed enough of the week's game planning that Case Keenum is expected to start, with Bagent as the backup.
events.so_what: Nothing here is startable at QB. A Keenum start caps the Bears' passing game for a week, which dents D'Andre Swift's receiving work and Kyle Monangai's scoring chances, and makes the Eagles DEF a strong points-allowed play.

events.headline: Travis Etienne exits vs. Raiders with a left hamstring injury, same leg that bothered him in practice
events.detail: Etienne pulled up after a 16-yard third-quarter run, grabbed the back of his upper left leg and went to the locker room. The Saints listed him questionable to return and he did not. He led New Orleans with 13 carries for 57 yards before leaving. Kellen Moore confirmed it is the same leg that gave him discomfort earlier in the week, before he was cleared with a full Friday practice.
events.so_what: A recurring hamstring is the kind that lingers, so treat Week 4 as doubtful until practice reports say otherwise. Alvin Kamara is the obvious beneficiary of the early-down work; check which of Kamara, CJ Donaldson and Kendre Miller is available on your wire before Tuesday bids.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley cleared, no designations for Monday at Chicago; Hollywood Brown out
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 and Sept. 25 items. Smith (hamstring) sat Thursday, was limited Friday and practiced fully Saturday, and he carries no game status for Monday night. Barkley (stinger) is also off the report. WR Marquise Brown is out, and TE Dallas Goedert (MCL sprain) is out and expected to miss a few weeks.
events.so_what: Both are starts. The Monday-night scare is over, so there is no need to hedge Smith with a Sunday-afternoon alternative. With Hollywood Brown and Goedert both out, fewer pass catchers compete for Jalen Hurts targets. Tank Bigsby goes back to handcuff status.

events.headline: Brock Bowers questionable at New Orleans; Friday DNP was a 'planned day off'
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 item. Bowers (knee, meniscus surgery before Week 1) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, then held out Friday on what Klint Kubiak called a planned rest day. He is questionable and Kubiak is optimistic he plays. QB Aidan O'Connell has since been ruled out for a personal matter, so Kirk Cousins starts again with Fernando Mendoza as the only other active quarterback. Kickoff is 3:25 CT, so the inactive list comes about 90 minutes earlier.
events.so_what: Leans toward his season debut. The coach sounds confident and nobody schedules a workout to settle it, but a first game back from knee surgery may bring a snap limit. Start him if he is active; Michael Mayer is only a start if Bowers is ruled out.

league_notes.hbgbs: Bowers is bwalsh89's; Mayer is Stipe's.
league_notes.pit: Bowers and Mayer are both tyanserg's.

events.headline: Broncos place Jonah Coleman on IR with a high ankle sprain; earliest return Week 7
events.detail: Rookie Coleman, ruled out for Sunday night against the Rams, goes to injured reserve with a high ankle sprain and must miss at least four games, making Week 7 against Arizona the earliest return. He had 58 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey carry the backfield in the meantime.
events.so_what: Coleman is an IR stash, not a bench spot, and only worth holding if your league's IR slot is open. Dobbins and Harvey split the work for at least a month, with Dobbins the steadier start.

events.headline: Commanders rule out surgery for Jayden Daniels; week-to-week in a brace, but Rapoport calls Week 4 unlikely
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. After specialist visits in New York and Los Angeles, GM Adam Peters said surgery is not on the table and IR has not been discussed. Daniels is week-to-week and will play in an elbow brace when he returns; the team's reported window is within about four weeks, with the first real decision before Week 4 against the Colts in London. Marcus Mariota starts Week 3 against Seattle. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports Daniels is unlikely to play Week 4 against the Colts, though the team is optimistic he misses fewer than four games.
events.so_what: The season-ending outcome is off the table, which is the big change: Daniels is a hold, not a drop. He still misses Week 3 and probably more, so a roster leaning on him needs a quarterback for the next two to four weeks. When he is back, a braced non-throwing elbow is the thing to watch for whether he keeps running, since the rushing yards are most of his konami-premium value.

events.headline: Jaylen Wright doubtful vs. Chiefs with a stinger and foot injury; Ollie Gordon backs up Achane
events.detail: Wright was limited Wednesday and Thursday, did not practice Friday, and is listed Doubtful for Sunday at Kansas City after the stinger he suffered in the Week 2 loss to San Francisco plus a foot issue. De'Von Achane has played 83 percent of Miami's offensive snaps through two weeks; Ollie Gordon is the favorite for whatever work Achane leaves, with Carlos Washington Jr. or Jarquez Hunter a possible practice-squad elevation.
events.so_what: Wright was a backup behind a back on the field for 83 percent of snaps, so nothing much changes for Achane, who stays a locked-in start. Gordon picks up the short-yardage and change-of-pace work, which in this format means a touchdown-dependent dart, not a flex.

events.headline: Texans rule Nico Collins out vs. Colts, his second straight missed game
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 item. Houston ruled Collins (hamstring) out Friday after he missed every practice this week. In Week 2 without him, Dalton Schultz caught 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards, while Xavier Hutchinson managed 3-37 on nine targets.
events.so_what: Bench Collins. Schultz is the Texans pass catcher to start. Hutchinson gets the volume but has not turned it into production, so he is a deep-league flex rather than a FAAB priority.

events.headline: Puka Nacua doubtful for Sunday night at Denver; McVay expects him back Week 4
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 24 item. Nacua (hip, described by McVay as groin soreness) did not practice all week and is doubtful for the Sunday night game against the Broncos. McVay said he expects Nacua back for Week 4 barring a setback. Without him in Week 2, Davante Adams drew 32% of the targets and TE Terrance Ferguson 29%.
events.so_what: Doubtful is effectively out: sit Nacua. Adams moves up as the lead target and Ferguson is a streaming TE for teams without an elite one. The Week 4 return estimate means Nacua is not a sell.

events.headline: Jaxson Dart undergoes season-ending knee surgery; Jameis Winston is the Giants starter
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 22 item. Dart had season-ending surgery Wednesday and the Giants formally placed him on injured reserve Thursday; the damage includes the MCL, PCL and meniscus, with no ACL involvement. Jameis Winston was already named the starter going forward, beginning Week 3 at home against Tennessee. Malik Nabers' right shoulder popped out in the same Monday night loss to the Rams; he popped it back in and returned, and no further diagnosis has been reported. On Wednesday the Giants listed Nabers as limited with the shoulder (an estimated report, since they held a walkthrough), with no quotes on his status.
events.so_what: No longer a planning question: Dart is done for 2026 and the Giants' rushing-QB premium goes with him. Winston throws more and riskier balls, which can mean more volume for Nabers and the other pass catchers alongside more drive-ending interceptions (only a point each here). Nabers being limited rather than out on the first report is a mild positive; watch Friday's designation before locking him in.
